newsitem.title: USA: AOL, Tel-Save reach long-distance deal.
newsitem.headline: AOL, Tel-Save reach long-distance deal.

text.p: Tel-Save Holdings Inc. reached an exclusive, multiyear agreement with America Online Inc. to offer low-cost long-distance telephone service to the huge online service's customers, Tel-Save announced Tuesday.
The announcement prompted a jump in Tel-Save's stock, which rose $5.375 to $18.50 on the Nasdaq in afternoon trading. It was one of the biggest gainers on the exchange.

Tel-Save, based in New Hope, Pa., made an initial $100 million payment to America Online and will provide further payments based on a percentage of Tel-Save's profits from the arrangement, the telecommunications company said.

The service, which Tel-Save said will offer America Online members "one of the lowest long-distance rates in the industry," begins with a sample of the on-line service's members in early summer, and is to be offered to all of them in the fall.
Dulles, Va.-based America Online is the world's biggest online service with about 8 million members.
The arrangement is the reverse of what AT&T Corp. and MCI Communications Corp. have done: offer their long-distance telephone customers access to the Internet.
The deal with America Online also provides Tel-Save with exclusive rights regarding local and wireless services, which would be offered as a package when available.
Tel-Save said it would offer online sign-up and billing, with America Online customers enrolling online and being billed through their credit cards.
Tel-Save said America Online made a significant commitment to promote the new service to its members.
America Online rose $1.50 to $37 on the New York Stock Exchange.
